# ABCDE approach

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Emergency medicine > Treatment approaches and procedures > ABCDE approach*

[Original Article Link](/library/YI0nYh)

---

## Summary

The ABCDE approach is an almost universally applicable strategy for the initial assessment and resuscitation of critically ill patients. Systems are evaluated and managed simultaneously in the order of their potential threat to the patient's survival: <u>airway</u>, breathing, circulation, disability, and exposure. As a first priority, <u>airway</u> patency is assessed and secured as needed (e.g., using <u>basic airway maneuvers</u> or <u>intubation</u>). Breathing is often evaluated concurrently and treated with <u>respiratory support</u> (e.g., <u>oxygen therapy</u>, <u>bag-mask ventilation</u>, <u>mechanical ventilation</u>) as well as specific time-sensitive therapy (e.g., <u>bronchodilators</u>, <u>chest tubes</u>). The next priority is circulatory assessment and initiation of <u>immediate hemodynamic support</u> (e.g., <u>IV fluid therapy</u>, <u>vasopressors</u>) as needed. A rapid <u>neurological assessment</u> should be prioritized next to identify reversible or time-sensitive <u>causes of altered mental status</u> (e.g., <u>hypoglycemia</u>, <u>intracranial bleed</u>), <u>seizures</u>, <u>weakness</u>, or other <u>focal neurological deficits</u>. The final priority is rapid exposure of the patient's body to identify potentially hidden clues to the underlying cause (e.g., rashes, transdermal medication patches) and remove any inciting or aggravating factors (e.g., <u>allergens</u>, contaminated or wet clothing). For each priority, lifesaving treatment should be initiated without delay, even if a definitive diagnosis has not been established. To ensure optimal outcomes, a team of appropriately trained staff should be assembled as early as possible, and team management should ideally follow the principles of <u>crisis resource management</u> (<u>CRM</u>). Following initial stabilization, a <u>secondary survey</u> including a thorough history and examination is initiated and, if necessary, the patient is prepared for transport or handed off to the appropriate specialty service.




See “<u>Management of trauma patients</u>” for the ABCDE approach as applied in patients with acute injuries.
